newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut's CIS issues $23 mln Senior-Junior notes.
newsitem.headline: Beirut's CIS issues $23 mln Senior-Junior notes.

text.p: Beirut finance house Capital Investment Services (CIS) said on Tuesday it successfully closed a $23 million issue of Lebanese treasury bill-linked Senior and Junior Notes.
The issue was the biggest under a $100 million programme started in May 1994 and brought the total to just over $63 million, CIS treasurer Thierry Depolla said.
"We successfully closed the seventh series today. The issue is for $16,625,000 Senior Notes and $6,650,000 Junior Notes," he said.
The notes are issued against two-year t-bills issued in Lebanese pounds and currently yield 21.66 percent per annum. The previous series were against six-month and 12-month t-bills.

The Senior notes carry 13.5-percent annual interest compounded annually. The Junior notes have no interest but are leveraged against the U.S dollar-Lebanese pound exchange rate, with returns based on the pound's performance versus the dollar.
Depolla said the indicated return at a constant exchange rate over two years would be 38 percent per annum.
The Lebanese pound has steadily appreciated since October 1992 under Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri. From a low of 2,750 pounds to the dollar in 1992, it opened on Tuesday at 1,559.
Depolla reported "huge" interest in the issue from international institutional investors and said this was a sign of confidence in Lebanon's political stability after recent parliamentary elections.
CIS is arranger, service and placement agent for the programme with Royal Bank of Canada Trust Corporation Ltd acting as trustee and Royal Bank of Canada, London Branch acting paying agent.
